F383 Race HUD in the original's look: the OSD scene `Osd/dial2.pssg`, its fonts and animations read at run time (2026-10-18, Claude Code; owner-approved task). Details: docs/RACE_HUD.md section 6. Evidence: worktree gracious-wilson-34e056 `local/race-hud-look/` (`dial2-tree.txt`, `osd-dump.txt`, `decomp/`, `tex/` private texture decodes, `app/data/*.png` renders and logs, `checks/`).
- Research [D]:
  - `Osd/dial2.pssg` holds the whole HUD as one scene: 423 nodes (244 quads/meshes), 206 shader instances of 11 effect files, 53 textures, two DXT1 cubemaps, 101 Bezier animations with named time ranges, and the camera `camera_dialcam` (vertical FOV 12.3068 degrees at z 3320).
  - Stored positions are the groups' off-screen positions; the `on` ranges slide them in.
  - The five OSD fonts carry `NEFONTMETRICS`/`NEGLYPHMETRICS`/`NEGLYPHKERN`; `sceneconfig.xml` assigns each text node a font.
  - grid.exe (decompiled privately): the `aspectratio` attach plays the layout range named `%1.2f` of the aspect cut to three characters (0x8D5CB0); a missing name changes nothing (0x8D5900), so 20:9 keeps the 16:9 layout.
- Change:
  - grid-formats `osd`: scene, materials, meshes (float/half streams), cubemaps, animations (Bezier keys, ranges), camera, `sceneconfig.xml` text fonts, fonts with metrics and kerning. PSSG reader: `NEANIMKEYS` read as raw data.
  - grid-app `osd_scene` (+ `osd.wgsl`, `osd_display.wgsl`): the scene renders through its camera into a transparent image, drawn as the lowest UI node with premultiplied blending. The pause menu, post-race, front end and touch zones stay above it. Animation sampling, metric text layout, one shader for the effect families [I].
  - `race_osd` drives texts and ranges from the shared `race_hud::HudView`: lap group, position and split pills, dial (speed digits, gear, needle, red zone, lights, unit, odometer, pedals), countdown box, wrong-way pill, flag.
  - Authored minimap: the route line plus the original player and opponent markers.
  - The OSD is off in the pause menu, post-race, replays and the front end.
  - `race_hud` keeps the plain panels only as the fallback when the files do not load.
  - `tyre_smoke` now queries the ViewerCamera (a second `Camera3d` exists).
  - `tools/push_android_data.ps1` also bundles `Osd/` and the five fonts (about 3.6 MB).
- Authored layout: beyond 16:9 the groups follow the layout's own slope (297 units per aspect unit). With touch zones (P11) the minimap and dial end at 48 % screen height, and the help strip sits under the top buttons. Without touch, the help strip is a small bottom-centre line.

F381 Contact-pool slot template, default-setup retrial and live engine-block braking runs (2026-10-18, Claude Code; coordinator's follow-up to F377). Details: docs/BRAKING_REFERENCE.md "Setup wiring retried" and "Live engine-block runs (F381)". Evidence: main checkout `local/driving/braking-20261018b/` (live captures with the +0x1840 block, port replays, check logs), `local/driving/setup-F372/` (setup patches, replays, test logs).
- Port fix [V, static]: the original pool allocator `B19E20` builds every 0x80-byte contact slot with constructor `B0ECE0` (+0x1C/+0x20 = −1, bytes +0x0F and +0x24 = 1, the other documented fields zero). The port's slots were zero-filled, so a wheel-overtravel contact in a never-used slot kept +0x0F = 0 and failed with "unsupported contact-group impact record". New `contact_groups::EMPTY_CONTACT`, used wherever pool slots are created (single-car world, multi-car pool and blank overlay pool, geometry reservation, prop slots).
- Driving results do **not** change [V]: solo identity `grid-opponent-race ROOT CD01 BP01 1 11200 ai` (no DF01, no AI characteristics) sha256 aad9a07a…e41b, unchanged; 12-car `… 12 11200 ai` sha256 54abbecb…2a2b, unchanged. With the old wheel constants no overtravel ever reached a fresh slot. (Runs with GRID_DEFORMATION_PARAMETERS and GRID_AI_CHARACTERISTICS also set give different, deterministic outputs; with the template set back to zero the 12-car output is the same, so that difference comes from the environment, not the change.)
- Default car setup (`Car::configure_default_setup`, the F377 trial) retried with the template [V]: braking replays BA on 76.231 m with the setup against 76.234 m without (original 69.65 m), BA off 54.774 m both (original 53.31 m). The gap does not shrink, so the setup is **not wired** (coordinator's condition). Its three test failures: the assists matrix passes with the template; the deep authored wall no longer reaches the suspension-damage threshold (peak 0.67 × threshold with the original's 0.153/0.14 constants, 1.28 × with the old 0.3/400; no wall depth reaches it), an assertion that encoded the unverified constants; the autopiloted Long Beach Drift Battle lap is a real regression (the BMW stops at the hairpin wall, reverses and falls through the world at about (−523, 2.9, −241)). The patch with setup, template and test re-baseline is kept privately.
- Live runs [V], with the owner's permission (via the coordinator and in this session); research copy only (SHA-256 b1da1b2d…aece34a6), PID 40200, 03:00–03:12 UTC; the 19 user files were snapshotted, 12 changed, all restored and hash-verified; game closed with WM_CLOSE; Steam install not touched. Run 3 BA on: 69.50 m / 3.09 s (run 1 69.65 / 3.10); run 4 BA off: 53.49 m / 2.18 s (run 2 53.31 / 2.18).
- Engine block [V]: engine speed +0x1894 matches the port (idle 232.7; 690–800 against 630–790 while braking in gears 4–2). The front-axle force gap is present from the first braking frame with and without BA (−5882 against −5057 N); the rear axle agrees. Differing words: car +0x1898 (525 / 1250), +0x187C, +0x189C..+0x18AC, front wheel +0x110 (−45 / −20). Car +0x1864/+0x1880/+0x1884 are 1.0 in the original (engine reset `996C70`), 0 in the port; no direct-offset reader of +0x1864/+0x1880 exists and +0x1884 is read only by driver preparation, so they are unlikely to matter. [I] The gap is in the torque path to the driven wheels, not in engine inertia.
- Tools: `tools/analyze_braking.py --drivetrain` (speed, RPM, per-axle force and wheel speed every 0.25 s from onset).

F380 Solo-run frame profile and the phone's CPU light clustering (2026-10-18, Claude Code; coordinator's follow-up to F379 after the first phone log). Details: docs/PERFORMANCE.md "Desktop solo run". Evidence: worktree focused-torvalds-7a0b54 `local/perf/app/trace-solo-{gpu,cpu}-summary.txt`, `local/perf/measure/solo-*.txt`; trace JSONs deleted after summarising.
- Phone log F376 [V]: Bevy logs "GPU clustering isn't supported on this device; falling back to CPU clustering". Bevy 0.19.1 hard-codes that for every Android build (`make_global_cluster_settings`: `!cfg!(target_os = "android")`).
- New grid-app diagnostic `GRID_CPU_CLUSTERING=1`: sets Bevy's documented `GlobalClusterSettings::gpu_clustering = None` at startup, so the desktop takes the phone's clustering path (rendering only; logs `perf_clustering mode=cpu`). tools/chrome_trace_summary.py now also groups exclusive system time by kind.
- Desktop solo traces (Bevy trace_chrome, 1280 × 800, baseline preset, steady state) [V].
  - CPU clustering costs 0.34 ms of CPU per frame, against 1.16 ms for the GPU path's CPU-side work: clustering is not the phone's problem.
  - Render thread 8.8 ms per frame, against 5.8 ms main plus 1.1 ms extract; `drive_tick` 1.0 ms. Even solo, the render thread is the longest CPU path.
  - Work by kind (CPU run, all threads): batching/instance buffers 1.85 ms, mesh upload/allocation 1.82 (`allocate_and_free_meshes` 1.51), bind groups/prepare 1.28, specialize/queue 1.01, visibility 0.99, simulation 0.98, shadows 0.75, extraction 0.64, UI 0.61, pass encoding 0.59.
  - The GPU-clustering run was more disturbed (p95 29.7 vs 21.1 ms), so its totals are inflated.
- [I] A phone core 3–4× slower than an i7-12700 P-core puts the render thread alone at about 26–35 ms, which fits the measured ~35 ms frames.
- Per-frame mesh replacement [V code]: `source_trees` re-faces every foliage billboard mesh each frame, `tyre_smoke` rebuilds every smoke group mesh each frame, and `ground_detail::present` rebuilds whenever the camera moves past its threshold. Each is a free, reallocate and upload on the render thread. Graphics files, not changed here.
- Multithreading cannot shorten this much more: Bevy already runs render systems in parallel and pipelines the render thread. The levers are less render work: no per-frame mesh replacement, fewer shadow cascades or a smaller map on the phone, fewer separate meshes.

F378 Android window follows the native surface; optional refresh-rate hint, present mode and frame latency; display refresh rate logged (2026-10-18, Claude Code). Details: docs/ANDROID.md "Frame rate"; docs/SETTINGS.md `[video]`.
- Why: the owner's log from APK 7b3122337846 printed `frame_setup present_mode=Fifo physical=1280x800 logical=1280x800 scale=1 monitor_hz=[unknown]` on a 3200 × 1440 panel. Code reading [V]: the `Window` is created with the requested 1280 × 800; winit's Android backend ignores it and reports the native size and dpi/160 only through its own calls; nothing in our app synced them. Whether the window stayed at 1280 × 800 for the whole run is unknown [I] (that build logged once, early); if it did, the camera aspect was 16:10 on a ~20:9 screen and the swapchain below panel resolution.
- `android_display.rs` (Android only): each frame, if the Bevy window differs from `ANativeWindow` width × height or the density scale (`AConfiguration` dpi / 160), it sets both and logs `android_surface native=... density_scale=... window_before=... scale_before=...`. `render_height` (F375) then caps the 3D scene from the real size.
- Options, defaults unchanged: `[video] refresh_hz = system | 30..240` (`ANativeWindow_setFrameRate`, API 30, declared with `#[link(name = "nativewindow")]`; logs `android_frame_rate requested_hz result display_hz`); `[video] present_mode = fifo | auto_vsync | auto_no_vsync` (only modes with wgpu fallbacks; `auto_vsync` = FifoRelaxed, a late frame shows at once instead of waiting a refresh); `[video] frame_latency = 1..3`. On Android `frame_setup` adds `display_hz` from `Activity.getDisplay().getRefreshRate()` (JNI); winit always reports none.
- Log reading [I]: the 28 FPS driving stretches have 35.6 ms frames with a 36.8 ms maximum, which strict 60 Hz Fifo could not produce (33.3 or 50 ms only), so the panel may run at a higher or variable rate, or the CPU loop time differs from the present interval; the pre-race 32.4 ms / max 33.4 ms looks like 60 Hz halved. The next log (with `display_hz`, `android_surface`, `render_scale`) decides; Mailbox/FifoRelaxed or 120 Hz stay owner choices.

F375 Render-height cap for the phone (`[video] render_height`, Android default 1080) and render/screen sizes in the FPS counter (2026-10-18, Claude Code). The owner asked for a cap: above Full HD makes no sense on a phone. Details: docs/ANDROID.md "Frame rate"; docs/SETTINGS.md `[video]`.
- `render_scale.rs`: `[video] render_height = native | 240..4320`; default 1080 rows on Android, `native` on the desktop. When the window is taller than the cap, the ViewerCamera renders into an `Rgba8UnormSrgb` image of the window's aspect ratio (3200 × 1440 → 2400 × 1080) and a `Camera2d` (order 1, MSAA off) shows it full-window through a UI `ImageNode`; at or below the cap it renders straight to the window, so never above native. Recreated on window resize. Windowed runs only; `--render` captures are unchanged. Pure size and parse logic unit-tested.
  - **HUD, pause menu, touch zones and FPS text are scaled with the scene** (UI on the 3D camera, drawn into the image; the ViewerCamera is also `IsDefaultUiCamera`). Keeping them native would need every HUD module retargeted to the window camera; not done. Their on-screen size is kept: the touch-mode UI scale is now min(h/720, image/window height), and without touch mode the scale is image/window height.
- FPS counter: second line `render of screen` (e.g. `711x400 of 1600x900`); `frame_stats` ends with `render=WxH screen=WxH`; a `render_scale ... mode=...` line per change.
- Correction to F374: the present mode is Bevy 0.19's default `PresentMode::Fifo` (the enum's `#[default]`; desktop log `frame_setup present_mode=Fifo`), not AutoVsync. Strict vsync either way. The texture path is already logged at start-up (`texture upload: gpu_bc= gpu_etc2= path=`), so it reaches the Download log; the Adreno 740 is expected to report BC [I].

F368 P11 Android controls: tilt steering, on-screen pedals and buttons, the phone profile drives with them (2026-10-18, Claude Code). Details: docs/ANDROID.md "Controls"; docs/PLATFORMS_AND_INPUT_RESEARCH.md 7.7. Evidence: this worktree's `local/android-p11/` (checks/, renders, logs).
- All AUTHORED (GRID has no tilt or touch input); original rules reused where they exist:
  - `input.rs`: `Source::Touch` (0/1) and `Source::Tilt` (bi-axis 0.5 + 0.5·tilt); `ActionMap::touch`: pedals uniPos dz 0 sat 1 and buttons with the constructor defaults (the keyboard preset's calibrations, exact 0/1); tilt to Steer Left biLower / Steer Right biUpper dz 0.05 sat 1.0 (4CC630's steering values for controller types 1–3; the pad stick's 0.2 is for stick drift). The Advanced Controls overrides apply on top. Menu Back also exits a replay. Assisted steering class (keyboard/pad), 827D10 and the shift queue unchanged.
  - `tilt.rs` (pure): up vector from the game rotation vector or accelerometer; angle about the screen normal (lean does not steer); landscape inferred from gravity (135° flip threshold, no rotation API without JNI); flat phone keeps the last value; tilt = clamp((angle − neutral)/maxAngle); one-pole low-pass τ 0.05 s; neutral from the first reading, CENTRE, or `tilt_neutral`.
  - `touch_controls.rs`: zone layout and hit test (pure), Bevy `Touches` glue, UI nodes under the race HUD and pause menu (`GlobalZIndex(-1)`); drive layer GAS/BRAKE bottom corners, HAND, GEAR ± (manual only), II and CENTRE top centre, VIEW/LOOK bottom centre, a tilt bar; menu layer (paused, post-race, replay) UP/DOWN/</> left, OK/BACK right. At most 8 touches. In touch mode `UiScale` = HUD camera height / 720 (≤ 1).
  - `android_sensor.rs` (Android only): `ndk-sys` 0.6 ASensorManager on its own looper thread, `TYPE_GAME_ROTATION_VECTOR` 100 Hz (accelerometer fallback), off while suspended. `android::touch_screen()` from AConfiguration.
  - Settings `[input] touch=auto|on|off`, `tilt`, `tilt_max_angle` (30), `tilt_neutral` (auto), `tilt_smoothing` (0.05); printed only when set, so the desktop `drive_input` line is unchanged. `tools/push_android_data.ps1` writes them instead of `autopilot = on`.

The default build is unchanged.

Under the 500 MB target. Built in 873 s (grid-app crate and a Bevy re-link; the jni dependency rebuilt the android-activity chain once, 874 s).
  - Trim to Donington route_0 only not done: about 23 MB (under 10 %), would need a new desktop check.
- **First-run copy**: new `LauncherActivity` (launcher entry, Java) copies the assets to `Android/data/org.reassembly.grid/files/` with a progress bar, `.part` files and a `.bundle-version` marker (deleted first, written last); `settings.ini` only when missing; then starts `MainActivity` (no longer exported). Java rather than Rust: the GameActivity glue blocks the UI thread in `onNativeWindowCreated` until the native thread polls, so a copy before the Bevy loop could show no progress [S, android_native_app_glue.c].
  - [V] 7 JUnit 4.13.2 tests (`gradle -p android testDebugUnitTest`, desktop JVM). The real APK unpacked on the desktop by the same `BundleExtractor` (zip source): 382 files byte-identical to the staged folder (1.7 s). Desktop release binary on that folder, 600 autopilot ticks with render: log identical to the full install apart from timestamps/paths, drive samples identical.
  - `settings.ini` line endings follow the checkout (CRLF from git, LF after an edit): a 10-byte difference changes the bundle version and only causes one more copy. The loader accepts both.
- **Visible failures**: `android.rs` opens `Download/GRID-Reassembly/log-<time>.txt` through `MainActivity.openLogFile` (MediaStore, no permission on Android 10+, newest 10 kept) and writes every logcat line there with a time stamp; a panic hook and the `run()` error path call `MainActivity.showFatal` (JNI, `jni` 0.21.1, already in the lock for cpal), which opens `ErrorActivity` in its own process `:error` with the message and the log path. `MainActivity.onDestroy` ends the process when finishing (winit/Bevy cannot start twice). An Android-only check in `run()` says "no game data in …" instead of the bare "os error 3" that the desktop shows for an empty game folder [V desktop message].
  - [N] Not seen on a phone: no device or ARM emulator here. Java-side crashes before the Rust code starts reach only logcat.
- **Controls**: the owner wants only an APK with the P11 tilt/touch controls, not an autopilot build (coordinator, 2026-10-18). So `-BundleData` now stages with the new `push_android_data.ps1 -NoAutopilot`: the bundled `settings.ini` has no `[diagnostics] autopilot`, and the APK uses the code's default controls profile (P11 makes tilt/touch the default on a touch screen). The adb path keeps the autopilot. Desktop check [V]: that `settings.ini` gives `drive_input device=auto`, no autopilot. The script now writes `settings.ini` with LF always, so the bundle version no longer depends on the checkout's line endings. The autopilot test APK above was deleted and not handed to the owner; the bundled APK is to be built after P11 lands. Gamepad not done: gilrs-core 0.6.8 has no Android backend and winit 0.30.13 maps pad buttons to `Key::Unidentified` and drops axes [S, source read]; a bridge is input code (P11).

F359 P6: CD01 (body-contact sampling directions) comes from the Steam grid.exe alone; no unpacked image or desktop preparation step is needed (2026-10-17, Claude Code). Details: docs/CONTACT_DIRECTIONS.md; docs/PLATFORMS_AND_INPUT_RESEARCH.md section 7.4.
- Evidence [V]: read-only Capstone 5.0.6 trace of the unpacked image (bundled Python 3.12.14). Main checkout `local/p6-cd01/`: `trace_recipe.py`, `trace.txt`, `recipe.rs.txt`.
  - The original fills the 44 directions at startup in the `C7DAE0` static initializer and writes them to the zero-filled `.data` at `F5E1B0`. It is 344 instructions of pure data moves: `xorps`, `movss` and `movaps` through a 16-byte stack slot, with no arithmetic.
  - Each x/y/z lane is one 32-bit word or zero; w is always zero. That gives 119 word lanes and 13 zero lanes, from 55 distinct source words.
  - All sources are in `.rdata` (`0xC89000..0xDA59A4`), which the Steam file leaves in plain form; SteamStub encrypts only `.text`. The section tables of the Steam and unpacked files are identical.
- Decision:
  - (b): the traced instruction stream is kept as a public address recipe, `CD01_SOURCES` (44 × 3 addresses, no game bytes);
  - (a) rejected: the values are the 6 axes plus icosahedron-family directions, typed as about 6-digit constants with inconsistent rounding (0.309011/0.309013, 0.447216/0.447219/0.44722), so formulas cannot give the same bits;
  - (c) not needed.
- Port:
  - `grid_tools::private_parameters::contact_directions` uses the same build check and the BP01 file-word rule, and checks unit length;
  - `grid-private-parameters GRID_EXE BP01 DF01 [CD01]`;
  - app: `body_contacts = derive` / `--body-contacts derive`, with `settings::Private` now covering CD01. A path still works, and `GRID_CONTACT_DIRECTIONS` still feeds the tests and tools.
  - Shipped profiles (body-contacts, time-trial, race, race-istanbul, race-long-beach) use `derive`. The five launchers no longer require `local\body-contact-directions.bin`.
- Verified [V]:
  - the derived CD01 is 712 bytes, SHA-256 `ea8d8bff…79c7`, and `cmp`-identical to `local/body-contact-directions.bin`;
  - new tests: `contact_directions_equal_the_prepared_file` (byte for byte; skips without `GRID_GAME_ROOT` or the file) and `contact_direction_sources_are_rdata_words`;
  - scripted app run `--drive --body-contacts derive --body-events derive --drive-ticks 120` prints `drive_private_parameters kind=CD01 source=derived-from-grid.exe sha256=ea8d8bff…` and runs with body geometry (`local/p6-cd01/app-smoke.txt`).
- Checks before rebase (on d967f35, `local/p6-cd01/first-run/`):
  - `cargo test --workspace --release --lib --test '*' --bin grid-app --no-fail-fast -- --include-ignored` with absolute GRID_* paths: 524 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored;
  - Clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -D warnings: clean;
  - solo identity `grid-opponent-race ROOT CD01 BP01 1 11200 ai` (no DF01): sha256 aad9a07a…e41b;
  - grid-soak quick: 20/20, 100000 ticks.
- Checks after rebase onto cdfc790 (`local/p6-cd01/`): release tests 527 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored; Clippy clean; solo identity aad9a07a…e41b; grid-soak quick 20/20, 100000 ticks (`soak-quick-rebased/`).

F351 grid-soak residuals fixed: prop boxes as box primitives, road triangles with their 0.02 margin (2026-10-17, Claude Code). The F342 follow-ups: thin props driven into the ground and players falling out of the world. Details in docs/BOX_CONTACTS.md, docs/SOAK_TESTING.md "Residuals (F351)" and docs/DYNAMIC_PROPS_RESEARCH.md "Pieces pushed into the ground".
- Static evidence: read-only Ghidra 12.1.4 headless on a copy of the dynamic-props project, plus capstone 5.0.6 through the private pe.py, on the hash-pinned image. Pseudocode, scripts and traces are in the main checkout's private local/soak-residuals/ (decomp/b1..b7, scripts/, bin/ = the compared binaries, wip/ = trace and tried patches, runs/ = the soak runs and traces).
  - [D] B18E70 builds a 12 × 12 pair matrix. Every pair of convex kinds {0 box, 3 sphere, 4 capsule, 5 cylinder, 6, 7 mesh} goes to AE8AD0; packed road chunks (kind 11) are queried per triangle (AEA1F0).
  - [D] AE8AD0 = B7F740/B7F520 (B7EA60 distance, B7ED10 sampled penetration with ±direction and B's axes) → AEE640 → AE2FA0. B3D890 box features: the dominant-axis face, oriented above 0.99.
  - [V] Live original: all eight road chunk shapes in the 6 October read-only captures have +0x220 = 0.02. [D] B212D0 copies it onto AEA1F0's temporary triangle and widens the candidate bounds by it.
- Causes:
  - Players falling (seed 1087, both routes; reproduced exactly on the F342 build 4ffec8b): at 39-45 m/s into a tyre wall entity box, the port's per-triangle box query gave normals such as (0.61, -0.79, 0), up to 0.9 m deep. The car was pushed through the road and fell.
  - Boards into the ground (seed 12; seeds 1005, 1012, 1029, 1074 at the same spot): the 150 m marker's lower board stands 2.14 cm above the grass. Its 2 cm shell plus the port's zero road-triangle margin left it without a ground contact in its first step. A car still inside it (the break comes after the capped step, as in the original) pushed it 0.38 m down. The car's contact direction matches the original: its sampled penetration minimum is straight up.
  - Not the cause: AEA1F0's backface correction stays disabled in the original (B1AB30 rectangle is FLT_MAX; the only other +0x294 writer, B0AD10, is unreferenced).
- Port:
  - grid_world::box_contacts (new): AE8AD0 for a moving mesh against a static box.
  - convex_distance: distance, batch depth and penetration take a point set; B7ED10's extra axes; contact_triangle with a triangle margin. The triangle path keeps every operation.
  - contact_manifold: mesh_feature split out; polygons of any size; shape_margin.
  - packed_contacts: Settings::shape_margin; bounds widened by it.
  - entity_geometry: a BoxShape per prop box with its shell (ornament stand-ins 0); the packed box data is removed.
  - track: ROAD_MARGIN = 0.02 for road chunks. The boundary sheet, car-to-car and the diagnostics stay at 0.
- Tried and not adopted (BOX_CONTACTS.md, "Tried and not adopted"):
  - AE8AD0 for car against box pieces, with AE2FA0's two-body reference rule [D]; and summed piece-pair margins (B7F520 mA + mB).
  - They fix two board losses (seed 1056, main's 1062 inputs), but targeted prop chaos (1 car, seeds 1..80) loses 2 and 4 boards against 0 without them. At the port's fixed 16 ms step a car is 0.5-0.85 m into a new piece, and the smallest overlap is often vertical. The original steps once per rendered frame (6 ms at 165 Hz), with about a third of that overlap.
  - Decision made overnight, the owner's to revisit together with the world step. Patches: local/soak-residuals/wip/v3-commit.patch, v4-uncommitted.patch.
- Results [V], release, cargo/rustc 1.99.0:
  - Seed-1087 replays on 4ffec8b plus the box change: Nürburgring passes all 2404 recorded ticks, Donington all 6549. At the recorded Nürburgring pose, wall 1508 now pushes the car up (normal (0.0004, 1.0, -0.004), 1.08 m).
  - Main's seed-1005 inputs: identical up to the board's spawn at tick 8822. The board then falls to y -50.6 on main and comes to rest at y -15.15 with the margin.
  - Main's failing long-run inputs replayed on this build: 15 of 16 pass; 1062 fails on another path (6 breaks against 2), a board spun into the road by the triangle-soup car contacts.
  - Long soaks, seeds 1001..1100, props on, main 307fe9b against this change (the change's runs in two parts after a stop): Donington main 9/100, this change 2/100 (1056, 1099); Nürburgring main 7/100, this change 1/100 (1085, a tyre-stack piece). Every failure is a prop piece; no car fell; no world error, panic or hang. Grid-soak sha256: main 58dd2afa…2caf, this change 9a34103e…12f2.
  - Targeted `--cars 1 --chaos prop --ticks 8000`, seeds 1..80, Donington: main 1 piece fall, this change 0.
  - grid-soak quick on the rebased build: 16/16 (seeds 13-16 are Istanbul Park), also `--car bmw --opponent-cars lac,bmw` and `--opponent-cars bmw,lac`.
  - Solo-lap identity: `grid-opponent-race ROOT CD01 BP01 1 11200 ai` sha256 aad9a07a…e41b, laps 88.42029812185638 / 86.28228501935392, identical to main, on the rebased build.
  - Race changes, explained by first divergence (temporary per-tick pose prints and a margin toggle, removed):
    - 12-car Donington (12 12000 ai, DF01): byte-identical with the box change alone. With the road margin it first diverges at tick 2749: car 9's floor comes within 2 cm of the road near (677, -166), a light contact at most 4 mm inside the margin. The order changes at 8/9 and 10/11; car contacts 1604 → 1211; the winner's time is 2:57.968 → 2:58.016.
    - 12-car Nürburgring (14000 ticks): the box change alone first diverges at tick 3163. Car 10 drives over a flat close_drift_flag.max box and meets its 2 cm shell.
  - Tests: `cargo test --workspace --release --lib --test '*' --bin grid-app --no-fail-fast -- --include-ignored` with absolute GRID_* paths, rebased tree: 489 passed, 0 failed; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean (rebased tree). New tests:
    - box_contacts (3);
    - entity_geometry::a_car_deep_in_a_tyre_wall_is_never_pushed_down (recorded hull poses, both routes);
    - dynamic_props::every_brake_marker_board_touches_the_ground_when_it_spawns (fails on breakable 116 with a zero road margin).
- Failed along the way:
  - At first I took the board case for original-equivalent, before reading the live chunk margin.
  - The first rebase stopped because the worktree has no git identity; finished with -c user.name/user.email.
  - The project `cargo t` alias still collides with a user-level alias; the full command above was used instead.
- Open:
  - car against piece and piece against piece as AE8AD0, together with the world-step question;
  - the boundary sheet's and the car hull's own shape margins (both 0, not established);

The Lacetti and the BMW differ only in positions, FOVs and pitches. New reader `grid_formats::vehicle_views`; tree dumps with the new `tools/binxml_tree.py`.
- Static [D] (read-only Ghidra 12.1.4 headless on local/phase3/ghidra-project, hash-pinned grid-unpacked.exe; evidence main checkout local/cameras/):
  - parameter binders and vtables: Chase 0x7F31B0 / 0xD00278, Mounted 0x7F4BE0 / 0xD00008, Head 0x7F3A70 / 0xD00140; FOV is degrees, converted ×0.0174533;
  - profile key `current_camera`, default chase_close (0x5F1100): restored at race start, a hidden view falls back to the first visible one (0x582750); saved at race end, a reverse view saves its owner (0x584E70);
  - chase yaw lag (0x8114B0): integrate yaw, angularLimit 10 rad never binds after the ±π wrap, return rate |θ| · (lagMin + (lagMax − lagMin) · speed / 55.5554 m/s); close-follow height −5 × filtered slope (clamp 0.58, damp 0.08);
  - Mounted shift (0x822510): Δv / (dt · 30) in the body frame, clamp(−a · axisScale, ±maximumShift), first-order lag at movementSpeed;

F348 the original's in-race pause menu in grid-app (2026-10-17, Claude Code). Details, evidence and decisions: docs/PAUSE_MENU.md.
- Evidence [D] (static; private copies in the main checkout's local/pause-menu/):
  - the menus are defined in system/states.bin (GRID binary XML), not in the front-end .pssg files;
  - system/flow.bin is the state graph: it picks the menu per event type and says where each link goes;
  - labels are ids in language/language_eng.lng; the new grid_formats::language reads that table (LNGT/HSHS/HSHT/SIDA/SIDB/LNGB);
  - menu keys and repeat timing come from ActionMap presets 0 (keyboard) and 4 (XInput) and repeatSettings.xml.
- Menus ported, in the original's order:
  - races (Race Day flow `f_`, pause_mainmenu_free_race): Continue, Instant Replay, Restart Race, Options, Retire from Race;
  - free practice (test drive, pause_mainmenu_test_drive): Continue, Instant Replay, Restart Test Drive, Options, Finish Test Drive, Ghost Car;
  - overlay: Back (= Continue) and button3 Reset Vehicle; Yes/No confirmations with Yes as the default ([D] active_default);
  - Options: Sound Setup, Screen Setup, plus Advanced for wheels, with each screen's rows. Effects volume, lap timer/position HUD blocks, km/h or mph and the controls' dead zones/saturations work; the other rows are shown dimmed.
- Behaviour:
  - Escape/P (pad Start) opens the menu and holds every fixed tick (`Driving::paused`). Escape no longer closes the app; it is the original keyboard Pause key.
  - Restart (menu or R) is one function covering every car, damage, the shared world and props, AI drivers, race manager, standings, timing and the countdown.
  - Retire from Race and Finish Test Drive close the app, back to the launcher. Decision [I]: the original goes to its post-race screens and from there to the front end; the results screens are a later task and the app has no front end.
  - Reset Vehicle uses the F341 placement, through the new `player_reset::place`.
  - Menu presses clear the gear queue (pad A is also Gear Up).
  - Pad Y thumbs are now read flipped, as the original's +0x94 flag does and its biDirectionalLower menu/look bindings need [I]; nothing else read stick Y.
  - New settings keys: `[sound] effects`, `[osd] lap_timer`/`position`/`speed_units` (docs/SETTINGS.md). Menu changes are not persisted (the original autosaves its profile).
- Code: crates/grid-app/src/pause_menu.rs (state machine, UI panel, race actions) and pause_menu/race_tests.rs; small changes in main.rs (install, restart function, drive_actions, HUD options), input.rs (7 menu actions), settings.rs, engine_sound.rs, tyre_sound.rs; grid-tools player_reset::place; grid-formats language.rs; tools/scan_strings.py.

The getter returns `.ned` collision_main max Z (+0xED6C), min Z (+0xED88) and max X (+0xED70), plus the body offset +0x1630 on Z; only when +0xC7AD is set does it move the two points through the deformation lattice 0x9A39D0.
  - 0x402D20 then grows the box to cover the tyres. The wheel words +0x14E0..+0x154C are written by 0xA0EC80. Front and rear tests are exclusive, and so are the left and right width tests.
  - It stores +0x110 half width, +0x114 length (front − rear) and the bumper points centre + forward · front/rear.
  - Observed records copy these fields (0x777A80). Overtake 0x77BF4C, brake_for_vehicle 0x78F928, avoid clearance 0x799B30 and the avoid room check 0x797720 (own × 2.0 + other + 0.5) use own + other half widths.

F342 grid-soak findings fixed: Nürburgring races start, no retirement from 0/0 damage, kerb and prop falls (2026-10-16, Claude Code). Details are in docs/SOAK_TESTING.md "Fixes (F342)" and "Runs after the fixes", docs/DYNAMIC_PROPS_RESEARCH.md "Soak fixes (F342)", docs/CONTACT_REORIENTATION_RESEARCH.md "Degenerate displacement", docs/HANDLING_DAMAGE.md "Unit thresholds" and docs/RUNTIME_LIMITS_AUDIT.md R06. Every F326 finding was reproduced with its exact replay first (pre-fix builds in a scratch worktree), then rerun on the fix. Static evidence: capstone on the hash-pinned image via local/ai-overtaking/scripts/pe.py, the existing local/dynamic-props and local/behavior decompilations, new dumps/scripts/traces in local/soak-fixes/; soak runs in local/soak/fix-* and final-*.
- (1) [D] 0x7D3C40 passes the unnormalised entity matrix to 0x7CE490 -> 0x7CDCD0 -> B11F40 (only the render path splits off the row lengths). Nürburgring's 6 tyre stacks (72 pieces) have a uniform 0.9718 scale; the catalog now keeps the scaled basis and rejects only a degenerate one. Nürburgring races with body contacts start.
- (2) [D] Standard.hdm thresholds are 1.0; a damage level saturating at 1.0 gives 9C5B90's ramp 0/0 (0x9C5D27..0x9C5D78). grid.exe stores the NaN too, but its readers (0x9B2C5A/0x9B42CD `> 0.8`, cap readers 0x9B37F7/0x9B388B) compare with JBE and read it as zero blend. The port now uses 0 (effects and steering caps) instead of retiring the car; the per-wheel effect reader does arithmetic, so there zero is a recorded deviation. Seed 2177 on the pre-fix build plus only this change passes all 15 606 ticks.
- (3, 4, 5) Not a mesh gap. AEE640's small branch (0xAEEB40/0x4682A0, confirmed |a|^2 < |b|^2 -> a) orients by the degenerate displacement: an exact vertex-0 witness keeps a margin contact's inverted normal, rounding flips it, and a rounding-sized vector just above 1e-5 (one ulp is 6.1e-5 at 600 m) wins the normalised branch. Each publishes 0.3-1.45 m contacts through the car or piece. AEA1F0's backface correction would catch it but its B1AB30 extents stay FLT_MAX (only the constructor writes them). **Port deviation (F320, recorded; owner may want to confirm):** a displacement within 1e-5 or 32 ulps of its coordinates is degenerate and the other one decides.
- (4) Track body contacts now get a capacity per shape pair (props, boundary, each road chunk), bounded only by the pool, as the original's per-call manifold; before, a board leaning on a prop box got no road contacts. The solo pool grows 36 -> 64.
- R06: a piece 100 m below the lowest road chunk is held (`PropWorld::hold_lost`), so a lost piece can no longer reach the 1e5 domain and pause the world.
- Nürburgring with props reached 138 bodies / 749 contacts; the deformation-callback pools (owner/contact collection, response consumption) still had the 512 port bound and paused the world. Raised to MAX_WORLD_CONTACTS like F317.
- grid-soak: `GRID_SOAK_TRACE_BODY=I,J..[:FROM]` per-tick body trace.
- Tests: nurburgring_scaled_tyre_stacks_keep_their_placement_scale, saturated_damage_at_unit_thresholds_gives_zero_blend, orientation_swaps_witnesses_and_preserves_signed_normal_lanes (rewritten for the deviation), a_hull_against_a_prop_box_keeps_its_road_contacts (557 boxes), a_piece_lost_below_the_world_is_held_until_reset.

F339 detached parts and driving: bumpers cost nothing, the rear spoiler never detaches, wheels are the gap (2026-10-16, Claude Code). Static only; details in docs/MECHANICAL_DAMAGE.md section 5 (rewritten) and a correction in VISUAL_DAMAGE_PARTS_RESEARCH.md. Tools: Ghidra 12.1.4 headless, -readOnly -noanalysis on local/phase3/ghidra-project; capstone sweeps with tools/scan_code_displacements.py. Evidence in local/detached-parts/: scan-01..06, dis-01/02, ghidra-01..06, and part-names.txt (the full E4EF20 id table).
- [D] All callers of the part lookup 98BFE0 were classified. Only 9C5B90 and 9C50C0/9F3E80 affect driving: exhaust 0x1F and rear spoiler 0x46/0x45, both already ported.
- [D] The remaining readers are rule, hinge or presentation code: 9EC9B0/9FF4F0 rules, 9DB0E0 hinges, 9E99B0 mirrors and windscreen, A18460 → +3A38 → 9CB5B0 (dangling bumper_bm node), 9F9BA0 joint matrices, and 920D30..921080/928680 debris-body positions.
- [D] No handling, aero, drag, mass or collision-shape code reads bumpers 12–17, the bonnet, boot, wings or doors. Bumper detachment has no driving cost.
- [D] The rear spoiler cannot detach in single player:
  - +1C88 is read only by the loader (9F11F8);
  - no rule pushes 0x45/0x46;
  - the loose-part timer needs state 2, which the spoiler never gets;
  - the resets set state 4 then 0 inside the same call.
  The +3BC grip loss and the SpoilerSeparation/SpoilerDangling sounds are therefore reachable only through network state or the state-5 list. F307's "9AE8F0/9E2AD0/9AEC60 read the spoiler level" was a displacement collision (9AE8F0 is a wheel-load split).
- Statuses (9DC270) [D/I]:
  - 0: attached;
  - 2: loose;
  - 4: detached, with a debris body at record +64 (mirrors follow a door);
  - 5: written only by 9EC950 from the parts +890 id list (count at +A0). That list is the vehicle wrapper's +14 block, a 0xCC90-byte copy made by A100A0 when a source is given, and it is re-applied by repair 9FF170 and re-attach 9FF3E0. [I] It restores a vehicle snapshot; it is not race damage.
  - A 40-entry request queue (9AB790 → 9DCFA0) carries network (9D77B0, 92E440), repair (5EC370) and hinge requests.
- [D] The driving-relevant detachment is the wheel:
  - 9EC9B0 sets car +22E4..+22E7 when the zone is above m_wheel_detach_level × S (Lacetti 27360 per tick); 996F60 is a second setter;
  - the port already consumes the flags (wheel_contacts, vehicle_sync, vehicle_handling, vehicle_manager), and 9E65B0 → 9E64E0(4, wheel) makes a lost wheel terminal damage;
  - nothing produces the flags in the port (grid-app damage_parts excludes wheels and is presentation-only).
- Also found, not ported:
  - 9FF4F0 detaches a loose part after a time at speed (car +1648 against CB093C/CB51B0/CB0D94);
  - wipers 0x5C/0x5F detach when car +C8A0 is set (windscreen smashed).
- Decision: no code change. The handling query stays None, which matches the original for every single-player car whose `exhaust` (0x1F) part never detaches; the Lacetti's exhaust is exhaust_bl (0x65). No cargo checks were run: no source changed. Playable not rebuilt; no input was sent to the original.
- Next:
  - port the 9EC9B0 zone classifier and wheel rule into grid-world for every car, so the existing +22E4 consumers fire, with grid-app reading the simulation's decisions;
  - check the BMW 320si (F338) for an `exhaust` 0x1F part with non-zero exhaust loss.

Code:
- grid_formats::ai: catchup.xml and ai_choreographer.xml readers with the built-in defaults and quirks (rev_length 10, min_sleep_distance ignored).
- New grid_tools::ai_pacing::Field, the race manager. It runs before the AI update and needs a reference (human) car. It provides:
  - conveyor belt;
  - race-start factors 1.05/B=1 (first 100 m) and grip 1.25 (first 750 m);
  - off-line grip assist;
  - lapping yield;
  - choreographer triggers and a single-event runner (MT19937);
  - catch-up, AUTHORED default rd_3_star.

- ai_driver, in a separate impl block:
  - Pace (A, B, backwards, damage gate, failures);
  - the mistake slot (arming, activation sites, 3/5 s, 60 s timeout, grip/brake/throttle effects, cancel at 10 m/s; random generator ported but off as in the data);
  - lost_control (crash/wobble);
  - controlled_stop (hook only);
  - race_damaged;
  - the retire failure branch with a removal request;
  - let-pass;
  - S = max(A·ratio, B).

F335 ETC2 texture cache for GPUs without BC (P8 follow-up, owner request) (2026-10-16, Claude Code). Details are in docs/PLATFORMS_AND_INPUT_RESEARCH.md 7.3.
- Without BC, a GPU with ETC2 now gets textures from a private KTX2 cache instead of the 6.5× RGBA8 decode. Path order: BC, then ETC2, then RGBA8. P5's diagnostics key texture_fallback is now off/on=rgba8/etc2 (legacy GRID_TEXTURE_FALLBACK=1|rgba8|etc2); docs/SETTINGS.md updated.
- New grid_formats::etc2: our own ETC2 RGB8/RGBA8 (EAC alpha) encoder and decoder covering all five RGB modes (individual, differential, T, H, planar), with steering bits for T/H/planar. No new crate. ETC2 was chosen over ASTC because no maintained pure-Rust ASTC encoder was found (web search 2026-10-16).
- New grid-app texture_cache: decodes the BC levels, encodes each level in parallel and writes `<fnv64 of DDS>-<len>-v1.ktx2` to settings::data_dir()/texture-cache (local/texture-cache in the checkout). Later loads go through Bevy's KTX2 loader, already enabled by the `3d` feature. Textures with any non-opaque texel use RGBA8 + EAC; otherwise RGB8.
- [V] On the i7-12700's Intel UHD 770 iGPU (Vulkan, WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME), which exposes ETC2 and ASTC; the RTX 4070 has neither. Evidence: worktree local/texture-fallback/etc2/.
  - Texel memory equals BC: car 9.29 MB, Donington 46.67 MB, 12-car race 92.14 MB (BC 91.40, RGBA8 593.12).
  - Frame PSNR against BC on the same GPU: car 50.8, Donington 45.3, race 43.9 dB. Cold and warm cache renders are byte-identical; there are no visible artefacts.
  - Load: race cold 9.2 s (encode 8.0 s, all threads, 16 other compile processes running), warm 0.46 s. The cache is 495 files, 78.4 MB.
  - Forced ETC2 on the RTX 4070 falls back to RGBA8 and logs why.
- New asset test etc2_quality_on_installed_textures (455 textures: Lacetti, livery 00, Donington tracksplit and objectstextures): overall 36.49 dB, worst 28.65 dB (a decal normal map); single-threaded encode about 10–12 s.
- New unit tests cover the codec, Bevy reading our KTX2, threaded = single-threaded encoding, and path choice.
- Checks: clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace --release -- --include-ignored with absolute GRID_* paths: 392 passed, 0 failed (rebased on a7f7112); cargo/rustc 1.99.0.

F332 reset and respawn: the original never respawns AI cars; the field gets past a held car with avoid and recovery (2026-10-16, Claude Code). Details are in docs/RESET_AND_RESPAWN_RESEARCH.md.

Static research (Ghidra 12.1.4 headless, read-only; private decompilation in local/ai-avoid-recovery/decomp/r1..r13):
- [V] AI cars are never reset. The only AI reset request (recovery timeout, req+0xB0 → packet +0x20) is gated by rcResetAllowed, which is false.
- [V] A stuck AI car retires: 20 s within 5 m, no racing car within 100 m. It stops with force brake and no steering.
- [I] The retired car stays in the world: no code was found that removes or ghosts it. req+0x38 is set below 0.5 m/s, but its reader was not found.
- [V] The game's only reset path is the player-only ResetLinesManager (race+0x22B0, ctor 0x612870, update 0x612C90).
  - Auto-trigger 0x60D590: |v| + |ω| ≤ 0.8 and up.y ≤ 0.17 for 2 s fires once. The pause menu's reset_car is another requester.
  - The reset fades out. vehicle+0x2C90 vfunc +0x38 is called with 1 until placement and 0 after.
  - Placement 0x9145D0 puts the car at the player's track-tracker point, heading along the line, with an upper Y of max(p.y + 1, ground + 1).
  - It uses the grid-spawn setter 0x9EF040: ground placement 0x9DE4E0, zero linear and angular velocity, wheel spin 0, gear re-chosen.
  - No separate no-collide period after placement was found.
- [V] Correction to F323: the "car 7 behind held car 5 moved 0.0 m" observation came from that test's fixed-throttle controls with no AI driver. It is not a missing respawn.

Port decision:
- No AI respawn.
- A car retired by F323 stays held as an obstacle, as the original leaves retired and wrecked cars standing. AUTHORED: the hold is instant, with no braking phase.
- Followers free themselves with the ported F301 avoid and recovery behaviours. MultiRuntime::obstruction already counts cars below 2 m/s, so held cars count.
- No engine behaviour changed.

F326 headless chaos soak harness: grid-soak (2026-10-16, Claude Code). Details are in docs/SOAK_TESTING.md. New `grid_tools::soak` (Session mirrors grid-app drive_tick/drive_actions R as of F323: player runtime built as the app does and swapped into slot 0 of the shared world, countdown hold with AI grid revving, AI opponents with the app's seeds and characteristics, dynamic props; seeded SplitMix64 chaos player with autopilot/random/full-lock/prop/wall/ram/off-track/reverse/spin/stop modes, random resets and manual shifts; scenario header and per-tick input records; app-log parser) and `grid-soak` (quick = seeds 1..12 x 5000 ticks, about 1 min; long = seeds until --hours; run; replay; replay-log). Each scenario runs in a child process under catch_unwind on a 64 MiB stack; failures: world-error, car-retired (F323 S3), panic, non-finite pose/velocity of any body, out-of-bounds (25 m/s fall or outside Track::bounds + margins), implausible speed, setup, crash, hang. Reports (seed, scenario, tick, error, all world bodies, last 64 player samples) and inputs under ignored local/soak/; summary.md groups failures by text. grid-app --drive now logs `drive_replay` (route, opponents, grid position) and `drive_input` (player's final controls, gear request, hold) on change; main.rs +33 lines (the gear request recorded is the one the F325 action layer applies to a manual gearbox). Small additions: Track::bounds, Debug on Controls, workspace profile `soak` (release + overflow-checks + debug-assertions). Verified: replay is exact (same tick and FNV digest); the owner's log manual-23606-10155 (old format, from drive_sample control changes) replays headless to "tick 2188: invalid contact-group counts or selector" with 268/268 logged poses bit-exact on c8ea239, and `grid-soak run --seed 1 --chaos prop --ticks 4000` reproduces the 16-body failure there at tick 1645 (17 bodies); on main after F317 both pass. Scripted grid-app runs (4 cars on F318, 6 cars manual gearbox on F323) replay with 60/60 and 78/78 poses bit-exact. Findings (none fixed here): (1) every Nürburgring scenario with body contacts fails at set-up, "scaled prop piece placement" (dynamic_props::Catalog::read), so a Nürburgring race cannot start; (2) Nürburgring 12 cars, AI car 6 at about 58 m/s: "nonfinite handling effects" (vehicle_handling.rs), a race pause on F318 and a retirement on F323, long seed 2177; (3) Nürburgring cars fall through the road at about x -210..-225, z -20..-45 (48 of 234 props-off runs); (4) Donington prop pieces sink through the road at x -390..-570 (62 of 248 runs); (5) Donington cars, mostly the chaos player, fall through the world (11 of 248); (6) 13..20 cars are refused at set-up (expected). Runs (main checkout local/soak/): long-1 91.6 min, 532 scenarios, 3.69 M ticks; long-nurburgring (props off) 82.6 min, 234 scenarios, 3.57 M ticks; quick runs on F318, F323 and F325 (same groups), app recording round trip 78/78 on F325; every recorded failure replayed on f6087f8 with the same tick and digest. Overflow profile: quick on both routes, no overflow panic (the code has no debug_assert!). A throwaway probe of 15 000 seeded mutations of five purchased files through binxml/progress/cqtc/ornaments/pssg readers gave 0 panics, so proptest-style parser fuzzing has low yield; the proposal ranks world-step properties (failed tick leaves state unchanged, reset restores, determinism) first. Bugs in the harness itself found and fixed during the work: long mode ignored --hours with --seeds; --keep was wired to continue-after-error; replay did not create --out. Checks: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings; 359 tests on 6234931 (F325) incl. asset (--include-ignored, absolute GRID_GAME_ROOT/GRID_CONTACT_DIRECTIONS/GRID_BODY_EVENT_PARAMETERS/GRID_DEFORMATION_PARAMETERS), cargo/rustc 1.99.0. Not rebuilt: the playable. Next: fix (1)-(5) with the replays; run `grid-soak quick` before pushes and `grid-soak long` overnight.

F325 input abstraction and gamepad (P1, P2) (2026-10-16, Claude Code). Details are in docs/PLATFORMS_AND_INPUT_RESEARCH.md 7.1.

Every device now goes through the original action layer and the human record. The keyboard's driving output is unchanged, bit for bit.

Code:
- New grid-app input.rs:
  - the 23 original actions;
  - bindings {source, calibration}, with the calibration ported exactly from AD9AD0/AD9A80 (SSE f32);
  - the action value is the maximum over the bindings, starting at 0; "down" is threshold <= v; pressed edges as in B7C120;
  - the 827D10 record: throttle and brake clamped, handbrake > 0.5, steering SteerL - SteerR (port sign, computed as before), Gear Up/Down edges and the last direct gear.
- input::sample runs in PreUpdate after InputSystems. The frame's gear edges go into ShiftQueue (AUTHORED bound 8), and drive_tick pops one per fixed tick. This fixes the just_pressed-in-FixedUpdate double or lost shift. Pause and Look Back also go through the action layer.
- New grid-formats action_map.rs reads the ActionMap preset XML.
- [D] New finding: the binding defaults come from constructor 8400B0 (uniPos, dz 0.2, sat 0.8, threshold 0.5).
- [input] settings, from --input SPEC or an [input] section of the --assists-file:
  - device=auto|keyboard|pad|wheel; keyboard and pad give Assists.input Keyboard (+E6C 1), wheel gives Wheel, auto keeps --assists input;
  - steering/accelerate/brake deadzone and saturation overrides (654C20/81CD30); dz >= sat is refused.
- Gamepad:
  - Bevy Gamepad through gilrs 0.11.2 (WGI on Windows);
  - GamepadSettings are set to pass-through on connection (dead zones 0, change thresholds 0, no trigger rounding);
  - sticks 0.5 + 0.5x; triggers and buttons 0..1;
  - the pad bindings are read at runtime from the user's own ActionMap/actionMapPreset4.xml (schemeType xinputScheme checked; never copied) and merged with the keyboard map.
- AUTHORED device guard: gilrs maps a wheel's axes by index, so its pedals could arrive as triggers. With device=auto, only names that look like gamepads are used; wheel or joystick names and the Fanatec/Thrustmaster/Moza vendor ids are ignored. device=pad accepts any device. Each connection is logged as drive_input_pad (preset4=used|ignored(reason)).
- Rumble is not sent (stub until P4).
- Play GRID Prototype.cmd passes GRID_PLAY_INPUT as --input and lists the pad controls.

F323 failure containment: one car's tick failure retires that car, and the race goes on (S3: R02, R16, R09) (2026-10-16, Claude Code). Details are in docs/RUNTIME_LIMITS_AUDIT.md S3 "Status (F323)". Before this change, any Err from one car's stage inside MultiRuntime::tick propagated with `?`. grid-app then paused all 12 cars, and R threw the race away.

Now MultiRuntime::tick contains each car's own stages: controls (staged_car), the vehicle manager, the car's track contacts and car-pair hull contacts inside the geometry provider, body events, and lap timing. A failing car keeps its previous state. From then on its world body is held at the last committed kinematics: body words 0x1C0..0x230 (mass centre, pose, angular and linear velocity), with both velocities zeroed. The held car still collides with the others. Its static contacts are skipped, and its Runtime::ticks clock keeps running. MultiRuntime exposes retirement(i) (tick and error) and newly_retired(). Shared stages (the world advance, prop pieces) still fail the whole tick atomically, as before. This is AUTHORED. The nearest original behaviour is skipping an over-limit island for a step (B7B850 status 1), and the original has no per-car retirement.

grid-app changes:
- A failing car becomes Out::Retired in the standings. The app logs one `drive_car_retired` line and the HUD shows "NAME retired: reason", or "Your car retired: reason. R restarts" for the player. The field races on. A retired car's engine throttle is 0.
- A world-level pause now shows "Simulation paused: tick N: ..." in the HUD instead of the generic text.
- A refused time-trial tick no longer pauses. It logs `drive_trial_event type=refused`, and the new grid-world State::skip_tick counts the lap as an invalid attempt and keeps the trial clock in step. When no lap is still timed, the runtime's current lap is marked invalid.
- A refused player dent projection keeps the previous mesh, as the opponent path does. One `drive_body_projection event=refused` line is logged per refusal kind, and the field is not projected again until it changes.
- Rate limiting: race reports count only the player's own body records (new MultiRuntime::body_contacts_of), not every contact in the field. The after-finish AI's continuous controls and a retired player's contacts no longer trigger a report.
- New `log_line!` macro (writeln! to a locked stdout, error ignored). It replaces println! on the per-tick and per-event paths: Driving::report, lap/trial/race-result/retirement lines, and damage, prop-break and audio events. Startup prints are unchanged.

F322 coordinate domains for large routes (S4: R03, A25, A27) (2026-10-16, Claude Code): docs/RUNTIME_LIMITS_AUDIT.md S4 and rows R03/A25/A27/B01/B02; docs/BODY_IMPACT_RUNTIME.md. Private listings and notes are in the main checkout's local/runtime-limits-audit/s4/. [V] Findings:
- 9E6660 (damage dispatch) compares only impact with mass x threshold and clamps the ratio to 1. It subtracts the car translation from the world point (subps 9E6731) and transforms the difference (770AB0) with no coordinate check.
- 999C00 works on the car-local point: enable byte, |delta| vs half-extent, radius, attenuation, clamp to 1.
- 9EF360 checks only the FLT_MAX impact sentinel, the B13/B14 flags (both non-zero gate the 9E6660 call), the +15A0 gate, the +2E8 timer, velocity^2 vs a constant and the suspension clamp.
- AE2FA0/B45310 (manifold) have only value/value compares and |dot| vs 0.99. B44E80 has no float compares; B444D0 none on coordinates; the kind-7 bounds B42050 seeds FLT_MAX accumulators with no domain.
So the port's 1000 m, 1e4 and 1e5 coordinate bounds are port guards.
Code:
- collision_damage.rs and body_impact.rs keep only finiteness for the point and car translation (the rotation <= 1.1, normal, impact and velocity bounds stay).
- The collision_damage settings-only damage_region pre-pass now uses the local origin instead of the world point, removing a hidden 1e4 world domain.
- contact_manifold.rs matrix and fallback point go from 1e4 to the 1e5 domain the same function applies to triangles and existing points.
- Mesh::world_bounds keeps its 1e5 guard, now documented in code as a port domain that only a lost body reaches (R06/R11: S1/S3).
Test: source_driving_body_events (asset) now checks that collision_damage at impact 0/1e4/1e8 (applied at 1e4 and 1e8) and body_impact give the same RNG and vehicle words (within 1e-3) with the car and point moved by (2928, 0, -2416) m, and that a tick with a body event 3.8 km from the car completes. F321 platforms and input research, ARM-ready reference arithmetic (2026-10-16, Claude Code): docs/PLATFORMS_AND_INPUT_RESEARCH.md (Android-first platform assessment, legal asset-import flow, original per-device input and force feedback, one input abstraction, 14-session plan P0-P13 with tilt-steering Android as the fun target). [V] Installed only rust-std aarch64-linux-android (rustup 1.29.1, toolchain 1.99.0; docs/TOOLCHAIN.md); grid-formats/grid-world/grid-tools pass cargo check and clippy -D warnings for aarch64-linux-android; grid-app stops at android-activity's activity-feature compile_error and, with bevy/android-game-activity, at the missing NDK clang (blake3, GameActivity glue); no NDK/SDK installed, no APK built. [V] Hard ARM blocker found and removed: reference_seed (34 files, ~40 sites incl. spawn, contacts, vehicle step, deformation) and engine-audio root used RCPPS/RSQRTPS and errored off x86. Exhaustive measurement on the owner's i7-12700 (family 6 model 151): RCPPS depends on the top 11 mantissa bits, RSQRTPS on exponent parity + top 10, 12 significant result bits; a pure 2x2048-u32 table emulation (FNV-1a-64 f8d5343dbccd59f9) matched both on all 2^32 inputs, 0 mismatches. New grid_world::sse_approx (unit test vs hardware), used off x86 and under validation feature soft-sse (grid-world; grid-tools forwards); SQRTSS -> f32::sqrt off x86; x86 default unchanged. grid-opponent-race release hw vs soft-sse: solo Donington 11,200 ticks laps 88.42029812185638/86.28228501935392 byte-identical output; 12 cars + DF01 deformation, 11,800 ticks, 827 contacts, all 12 per-car state hashes byte-identical (local/platforms/sse-approx/runs). Not run on an ARM device. Recommendation P1b (owner rule F320): make the table the default on all CPUs, since the hardware path makes results CPU-vendor dependent. [D] Original input (static, Ghidra 12.1.4 read-only private project copy, Capstone 5.0.6; local/platforms-input/ORIGINAL_INPUT_DEVICES.md): DirectInput8 + XInput 1.3, axes 0..65535 normalised, 8 action-map presets matched by exact product name (no generic fallback), calibration uniPos/uniNeg/biUpper/biLower with dz/sat, action = max over bindings; no keyboard/digital ramp at the input layer (port's keyboard path is ORIGINAL); keyboard/XInput pad/RumblePad 2 assisted, wheels unassisted with a ring + 7-slope latency extrapolation (not ported) and 828670 shaping; Advanced Controls wheelLinearity 14/20, dz/sat overrides, feedback_force/friction/effects 0.5; FFB = GameFFB thread (~100 Hz, Sleep 10) driving ONE DirectInput ConstantForce plus software damping (caster from front tyre forces, lateral/angle friction, surface/kerb/gear/skid/suspension/damage/collision samples from forcefeedback/*.xml), pads get XInputSetState from samples. Other findings: BC-only textures with a hard TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_BC assert (about 63% of Android Vulkan devices lack BC); install root, argv flags, env switches, .cmd launchers and CWD-relative writes are desktop-only; CD01 needs the Steamless-unpacked image (blocker for other users), BP01/DF01 can be read from the Steam grid.exe in Rust; libm-dependent sin/tan/atan/acos/pow calls can differ across platforms (P13); install 10,319 MB, one race reads about 100-130 MB; shift keys use just_pressed in FixedUpdate (double/lost shift risk). Gyro/tilt and touch HUD are AUTHORED input classes mapped onto the original pad semantics. Open: pad dead zone on a fresh profile, FFB snapshot writer, input vs substep order, device tests on a phone/wheel. Web research notes (Bevy 0.20 released 2026-10-08; cargo-ndk 4.1.2 + Gradle, NDK r30 LTS, gilrs has no Android backend, SDL3 3.4 LG4FF HIDAPI wheels) in the session notes folder; key URLs in the doc. F320 owner decision on the AI avoid leak (2026-10-16, Claude Code): the F306 port proposal (reproduce 0x79A530's rsqrtps f32 cosine and acos NaN, which makes multi-car results CPU-dependent) is NOT adopted. Owner: CPU-dependent race results are bad; stay close to the original's behaviour but without such bugs and leaks. The port keeps the deterministic documented rule (clamped exact cosine), so the 0.36% avoid leak is intentionally absent. Still open and deterministic: the from-gate normal t instead of the interpolated line direction (docs/AI_AVOID_RECOVERY_LIVE.md, Port proposal item 2). Docs updated; no code change. General rule from this decision: original bugs that make results nondeterministic or hardware-dependent are not reproduced; the intended behaviour is ported and the deviation is recorded.

F319 particle quad extent: the stored size is the half extent (2026-10-15/16, Claude Code): settles the F316 open lead. Full evidence in docs/TYRE_SMOKE_RESEARCH.md 4.3; summary in docs/GROUND_EFFECTS_RESEARCH.md section 2 "Particle size". Static only: capstone on the hash-pinned local/compatibility/grid-unpacked.exe (sha256 aac46a64...4f34514) via the private local/tyre-smoke/scripts pe.py/cs.py/calls.py, run with Python 3.14.4 -I. Dumps and helper scripts are in the main checkout's local/particle-extent/disasm/. [V] Findings:
- Update 8A9CC0 writes particle width/height to +0x20/+0x24 (0x8AB458/0x8AB477) with no factor 1/2. Renderer 886BD0 reads the same particle and builds corners from (+-w, +-h, 0) (0x88B3DB..0x88B7EE) times rows = spin R x billboard basis B (0x88ACDA..0x88AE00). It then applies the inverse node transform (0x88B1D6..), which the draw's world matrix cancels.
- billboardingType is emitter +0x84 (parser 0x8A4DBC: InverseView 1, CameraFacing 2, OrientationAligned 3, VelocityAligned 4, HorizonAligned 5, ZAxisAligned 6, VelocityFacing 7, VelocityFacingX 8). +0x188 is axisType (random3D 0, WorldSpace 1, ParticleSpace 2, SpeedSpace 3, parser 0x8A5A7C), not the billboarding type as earlier notes assumed.
- InverseView B = camera rows copied at entry from manager +0x19F100.. (jump table 0x88CC34 -> 0x886FF9). setCamera 868D60 fills them from camera +0x90... The race camera path 5FA440 builds them from three rsqrt-normalised vectors; 864770 only permutes and negates rows; 63A370 takes general inverses, which keep a rigid matrix rigid.
- CameraFacing and HorizonAligned B = look-at frame 4695B0: rows 0/1 = normalised crosses, so unit and perpendicular.
- Spin R = identity for |angle| < 1e-4, otherwise a Rodrigues rotation about axis +0x190, which is normalised at parse time (0x8A5D00..0x8A5D2F).
- [I] Other camera callers of 63A370 were not traced.
So the drawn edge is 2 x size: a K_Tarmac Smoke particle ends 4 m across, and a gravel stone is about 1-5 cm.
Code: crates/grid-app/src/tyre_smoke.rs and particles.rs now use the stored size as the half extent (previously 0.5 x size, i.e. half the original).

F318 runtime limits audit (2026-10-15, Claude Code): docs/RUNTIME_LIMITS_AUDIT.md (research and docs only; no runtime code changed). Read-only static inventory at c8ea239 of every per-tick failure path in grid-world, the grid-tools library modules used by grid-app, and grid-app (test modules and src/bin excluded): 721 Err( sites, 97 unwrap/expect, 508 integer casts, grouped into 184 rows (A01-A50, B01-B46, C01-C47, D01-D41), each with file:line, effect when it fires, race reachability, provenance and a ranked risk list (R01-R25 plus latent states). Original limits [V] from static analysis of the hash-pinned grid-unpacked.exe (pe.py/capstone, existing Ghidra 12.1.4 outputs, the existing read-only live snapshot local/world-settings/paused01.json; private evidence local/runtime-limits-audit/). The game code writes the per-island limits 200 bodies / 1000 constraints / 3000 DOF rows at 0x5F5F4B..57 (live world+788 = 200/1000/3000) and maxGeoms 11500 at 0x5F5E28. An island over its limit is skipped for that step (B7B850 status 1; optional farthest-first freeze B24EF0 when focus flag +11C is set, which is unknown live). Global pools are fixed free lists that refuse (AD9220). Waitable lists drop the item with error 0x21. Per-owner selection 80, response pairs 240, 20 contacts per collision, candidate grid 25. Skid marks steal the farthest active strip (73E430). Route scan (grid-binxml, read-only on the install): 34 of the 92 shipped routes have racing-line points beyond +-1000 m (Le Mans 2928, Haruna 2416, Spa 1463, Washington, Okutama, San Francisco, Detroit), so the port's +-1000 m point/pose guards in collision_damage.rs:36-57 and body_impact.rs:47-81 would pause on the first impact past 1 km there; Donington (795 m) and Nurburgring (851 m) are safe. Ranked open risks after F317: no per-car failure containment (one car's Err pauses all cars; R loses the race); the 1000 m damage domain on other routes; silent contact starvation at 12 cars (208 provider slots in car-index order); a falling piece that never sleeps reaches the 1e5 mesh-bounds guard about 150 s later and pauses every tick; about 120 finite/1e6 guards; a latched-Retire AI is never retired in the standings; per-contact logging grows the playtest log by hundreds of MB/h; asin domain on an exactly sideways slide (vehicle_step.rs:87); 100 km lap-timing bound with no respawn; manual gear presses read with just_pressed in FixedUpdate; all engines muted after the player finishes. F317 resolved the 16/64-body bounds (R01, R04). Corrections to work notes: armco and tyre walls stay static (only boards 2, tyre stacks 12, cushions 1 add bodies); physical_tick is test-only. The fix plan is grouped into sessions S1-S9 (S1 mostly done by F317). Not verified (static only; nothing built or run): Donington use of materials without mechanics (C13), the body-event contact window (C20), the live focus flag and original particle buffer counts.

F316 gravel debris size: the original never grows stones (2026-10-15, Claude Code): owner playtest of 7f22c32 reported dirt/gravel "splashes" as big flat 2D pictures. docs/GROUND_EFFECTS_RESEARCH.md section 2 "Particle size", docs/TYRE_SMOKE_RESEARCH.md 4.2. Static research on the hash-pinned grid-unpacked.exe (capstone via the private local/tyre-smoke/scripts pe.py, Codex runtime Python 3.12.14; existing Ghidra 12.1.4 output). [V]: parser 8A49A0 stores agescale initial/final width/height at emitter +1AC..+1B8, scaleVariance +1BC, growthPercentage +1C0, scaleType code +1C4 (linear 1 .. quadraticDecelerate 5, absent 0), raw; defaults 875620 = 1.0 and type 0. Spawn 890A10 draws a whole percent v in +-scaleVariance. Update 8A9CC0 (0x8AB3ED..0x8AB527): without scaleType, width = initial x (1 + v/100) x growth^floor(25 age) and finalWidth is never read; with one, lerp(initial, final, F(age/life)) without variance. So K_Gravel Large_Stones (LGDR, MGDR, HGDR, DGDR, GRAV, DIRT, TRAP; no scaleType) stays 0.015 m +-70 %. The F313 port lerped 0.015 -> 4.0 m, so opaque stone sprites grew to about 4-6.8 m within 0.8 s: this was the owner's artifact. finalWidth -1 occurs only on emitters that never read it. The tyre-smoke port already used this rule (unchanged). Frame frequencies are raw weights that the parser normalises; grid_formats::kickup already matched. Billboarding (InverseView), type lit/pfx_lit and opaque alpha match the port's approach; the original stones are flat camera-facing sprites too, just centimetre-sized. Code: grid_formats::kickup keeps scaleType, growthPercentage and drag rangeX with the original defaults; particles.rs applies the original size rule, alpha in/out in seconds [V, TYRE_SMOKE_RESEARCH 4.2; were life fractions] and the recovered drag 0.003*influence*rangeX*0.01 per second (was an AUTHORED 1/s); wheel_debris drops the -1 handling and applies the variance only without a scale type. New unit test width_follows_the_original_scale_rules. Validation (main checkout local/ground-effects/gravel-size/): LGDR located from route_0/track.jpk (7,078 LGDR, 6,217 MPDR triangles; temporary probe, not committed). Run --drive --drive-ticks 652/660 --throttle 1 --steering -0.02 crosses LGDR at ticks 636-660. Before = playable 7f22c32 exe copy (sha256 c34ffe711fc4...), after = this tree's release exe (b66da70bbc52..., unversioned). lgdr-before shows metre-sized brown stone sprites behind the car; lgdr-after shows specks; lgdr-side-* (GRID_EFFECTS_CAMERA) shows half-metre quads before. Grass (grass-side-*, tick 272, 400 emitted/169 live in both runs): small mud bits in both, visible longer after. Checks: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace --release -- --include-ignored with absolute GRID_GAME_ROOT/GRID_CONTACT_DIRECTIONS/GRID_BODY_EVENT_PARAMETERS/GRID_DEFORMATION_PARAMETERS: 335 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (local/ground-effects/gravel-size/tests-full-ignored.log). rustfmt --check clean on the changed files (pre-existing fmt drift in wheel_ground.rs and source_vehicle/assists.rs left alone). F306 AI avoid leak cause (2026-10-15, Claude Code): docs/AI_AVOID_RECOVERY_LIVE.md "The 0.36% leak". Static (pe.py/capstone on grid-unpacked.exe sha256 aac46a64...4f34514; Ghidra not needed) plus a reanalysis of trace-race-03; no live run, no input to the game. Cause [V code]: in 0x79A530 the angle test is an xz-only f32 cosine; its lengths come from rsqrtps plus one Newton step (0xCAF888 1.0, 0xCAF88C 0.5), which biases |cos| upward. 0xBF4067 acos returns NaN for |x|>1 (0*inf at 0xBF4499, no clamp), and comiss/ja treats NaN as not taken -> return 0 -> not excluded -> Branch A fires. The F302 emulation used a clamped double cosine. Evidence: tools/analyze_avoid_leak.py (sha256 1b847a6f...ff99913c6): all 70 TSV leak rows (the in-run counter said 71) lie within 5.1e-4 rad of antiparallel to the from-gate t; fire rate per 1e-4 rad bin 1.00/1.00/0.89/0.55/0.37/0.04/0; 0 of 19,447 frames beyond 7e-4. tools/avoid_leak_rsqrt_mc.rs (sha256 199c13f1...6f4438c7d, rustc 1.99.0) on the same i7-12700 with host rsqrtps gives 0.99/0.98/0.96/0.87/0.62/0.25/0.03/0, the same sharp edge about 1e-4 rad further out [I: pitch, w lane, sample timing]; exact or truncated rsqrt models do not match. 0x79EE30 order [V]: 0xAB87D0, view refresh 0x79C360, tests 0x79CAA0, controller 0x787620 (driver+0x3100, touches neither view nor records), vtable+8 of *(drv+0x9F8), 0x79E050; so stale data is not the cause. About 2.9 AI steps per trace sample (dt 0.00606 s vs 17.5 ms) [I] explains why leaks show as single samples. Port proposal, not implemented: f32 cosine with rsqrt-estimate lengths (_mm_rsqrt_ps on x86), raw r.forward, t from the from-gate normal instead of the line direction (gate normals deviate up to 0.25 rad), acos NaN = not racing. Solo 88.420/86.282 s are unaffected by construction (the obstacle exists only with other cars); multi-car results would become CPU-dependent like the original. Adoption is the owner's decision. Private MC output local/ai-avoid-recovery/leak/mc-host-i7-12700.txt. Docs updated: AI_AVOID_RECOVERY_LIVE/RESEARCH, AI_DRIVER_PORT. No port change, no rebuild, playable unchanged. Open: live confirmation logging raw record +0x30 and gate-normal bits; whether rsqrtps differs between P- and E-cores.

## Hypotheses and unresolved questions

- **H001, medium confidence:** the observed crash occurs in unsafe startup cleanup and may mask an earlier initialization failure. Do not call this the initiating root cause yet.
- Determine the first failed initialization operation before the apparent cleanup path.
- Establish whether CPU detection/worker scheduling, graphics-device creation, audio, overlays, an absent resource or another subsystem triggers that failure.
- An affinity limit may leave some CPU-count detection APIs unchanged; F008 does not rule out every CPU/worker-map defect.
- Lacetti/Donington pairing and route_0 reads are confirmed. Resolve the human-readable layout label, cached/shared dependencies and internal container consumption; do not treat the observed 130-file set as exhaustive.
- Identify the generic HID game controller and any wheel/pedal requirements when reference driving is available.
- **H002, provisional:** repeated display enumeration and/or instrumentation overhead may stretch startup well beyond the baseline. The short Procmon/native-debug probes do not establish which operation fails first.
- **H003, confirmed startup remedy in isolated copy:** process-codepage compatibility controls the observed startup failure. Paired manifest controls differ only in `en-US` versus `UTF-8` and show repeated survival versus the original exception (F018); owner confirms main menu (F019). The later `uk-UA` copy supports autosave persistence and driving. Exact initiating API/conversion and broader game-mode compatibility remain unresolved. No system-locale change/reboot made.
